Let $\mathcal X,\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be nonempty finite alphabets, let $p$ be a pmf on $\mathcal X$, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,\infty)$ be finite-valued. A test channel is a stochastic matrix $W(\hat x\mid x)$, and its expected single-letter distortion is $\sum_{x,\hat x}p(x)W(\hat x\mid x)d(x,\hat x)$, with block distortion as in [[def-it-single-letter-distortion-and-block-distortion]]. Put $D_{\min}=\sum_xp(x)\min_{\hat x}d(x,\hat x)$. Define, in bits,
$$
R_{p,d}(D):=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\min_{W:\,\mathbb E d(X,\hat X)\le D} I(X;\hat X),&D\ge D_{\min},\\[4pt]+\infty,&D<D_{\min}. \end{cases}
$$
The minimum exists by [[lem-it-finite-rate-distortion-minimum-attained]]. Values are not operational code rates; the finite memoryless coding theorem is a separate claim.

Let $\mathcal X,\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be nonempty finite sets, let $p$ be a probability mass function on $\mathcal X$, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,\infty)$ be finite-valued. Put
$$
D_{\min}:=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p(x)\min_{\hat x\in\widehat{\mathcal X}}d(x,\hat x).
$$
For every $D\ge0$, the feasible stochastic channels $W(\hat x\mid x)$ satisfying $\sum_{x,\hat x}p(x)W(\hat x\mid x)d(x,\hat x)\le D$ form a nonempty set exactly when $D\ge D_{\min}$. Whenever nonempty, mutual information in bits attains its minimum over this set.

Let $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ and $(\widehat{\mathcal X},\widehat{\mathcal A})$ be measurable spaces, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,+\infty]$ be a measurable single-letter distortion. For a positive integer $n$, define the normalized additive block distortion by

$$d_n(x^n,\widehat x^n):=\frac1n\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}d(x_i,\widehat x_i).$$

When the alphabets are finite and $d$ is finite-valued, define $d_{\max}:=\max_{x,\widehat x}d(x,\widehat x)$. Expected distortion is $\mathbb E d_n(X^n,\widehat X^n)$; the excess-distortion probability at threshold $D$ is $\mathbb P(d_n(X^n,\widehat X^n)>D)$. These are distinct criteria: one is an expectation and the other is a tail probability.

Let $p_{XY}$ be a joint probability vector on finite alphabets $\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y$, with marginals $p_X(x):=\sum_y p_{XY}(x,y)$ and $p_Y(y):=\sum_xp_{XY}(x,y)$. The marginals are probability vectors by [[lem-it-finite-marginals-and-conditionals-are-pmfs]]. The joint vector is the outcome-weight function of the canonical finite probability space from [[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]; its coordinate maps are finite random elements in the sense of [[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]. Define mutual information in nats by

$$I(X;Y):=D(p_{XY}\|p_X\otimes p_Y)=\sum_{(x,y):p_{XY}(x,y)>0}p_{XY}(x,y)\ln\frac{p_{XY}(x,y)}{p_X(x)p_Y(y)},$$

where $D$ is the finite KL convention of [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]] and $(p_X\otimes p_Y)(x,y):=p_X(x)p_Y(y)$. Every ratio in the displayed sum is positive and finite: if $p_{XY}(x,y)>0$, then each marginal sum is at least that positive entry. The sum is over finite support, so $I(X;Y)$ is finite. The base-$b$ version replaces $\ln$ by $\log_b$.

For finite $X,Y,Z$ with a joint pmf,

$$H(X,Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|X,Z),$$

and

$$I(X;Y,Z)=I(X;Z)+I(X;Y|Z).$$

In particular, $I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X|Y)=H(Y)-H(Y|X)$. All terms are finite.

For finite $X,Y,Z$,

$$I(X;Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|Z)-H(X,Y|Z)\ge0.$$

Equality holds if and only if, for every $z$ with $p_Z(z)>0$, the conditional joint pmf factors as $p_{XY|z}=p_{X|z}p_{Y|z}$; this is conditional independence given $Z$.

For any $b>1$, define each base-$b$ finite information quantity by replacing $\ln$ with $\log_b$ in its defining finite formula. Then

$$H_b(p)=\frac{H(p)}{\ln b},\qquad D_b(p\|q)=\frac{D(p\|q)}{\ln b},$$

where the second equality is in $[0,+\infty]$ and $+\infty/\ln b:=+\infty$. The same conversion holds for finite conditional entropy, mutual information, and conditional mutual information. In particular, values in bits equal nats divided by $\ln2$.

derivations.claim: Uniform time-sharing produces a finite test channel with source marginal P_S and expected distortion D_k.
The IID mutual-information chain rule and nonnegative conditional mutual information show I(S^k;S-hat^k) >= sum_i I(S_i;S-hat_i).

Time-sharing and nonnegative conditional mutual information bound the single-letter mutual information by the block value; feasibility and base conversion give ln(2)R(D_k) <= k^{-1}I_nats(S^k;S-hat^k).

Let $\mathcal S,\mathcal X,\mathcal Y,\widehat{\mathcal S}$ be nonempty finite alphabets, let $P_S$ be a probability vector on $\mathcal S$, and let $W$ be a finite discrete memoryless channel from $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal Y$ as in [[def-discrete-memoryless-channel]]. For positive integers $k,n$, a deterministic **$(k,n)$ joint source-channel code** is a pair of maps
$$f_k:\mathcal S^k\to\mathcal X^n,\qquad g_k:\mathcal Y^n\to\widehat{\mathcal S}^{\,k}.$$
The source block has law $P_S^{\otimes k}$, the channel output conditional on input $x^n$ has law $W^n(\cdot\mid x^n)$, and the reproduction is $\widehat S^k=g_k(Y^n)$. The code has no feedback.

A **code sequence at channel-use ratio $\rho$** consists of such codes with source lengths $k\to\infty$, channel lengths $n_k$, and $n_k/k\to\rho\in(0,\infty)$. In the lossless case $\widehat{\mathcal S}=\mathcal S$, its block error is $\Pr[\widehat S^k\ne S^k]$. In the lossy case, for finite nonnegative single-letter distortion $d$, its normalized block distortion is $d_k$ from [[def-it-single-letter-distortion-and-block-distortion]]; expected distortion and the positive-slack excess-distortion probabilities $\Pr[d_k>D+\varepsilon]$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ are distinct criteria.

For an input probability vector $P_X$ on $\mathcal X$ ([[def-finite-probability-vector]]), let $P_{XY}(x,y):=P_X(x)W(y\mid x)$ and $Q_{P_X}(y):=\sum_xP_X(x)W(y\mid x)$. Write $I(P_X;W):=I(X;Y)$ for this joint law, using [[def-it-finite-mutual-information]]. The **single-letter information capacity** is
$$C(W):=\sup_{P_X} I(P_X;W),$$
measured in nats per channel use. The finite-dimensional maximum is attained, as proved in [[lem-discrete-memoryless-channel-capacity-is-attained]].

A rate $R\ge0$ is **average-error achievable** for $W$ if there are length-$n$ codes for all sufficiently large $n$ with
$$\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{\ln M_n}{n}\ge R,\qquad \varepsilon_{\rm av}(n)\longrightarrow0.$$
It is **maximal-error achievable** if the same condition holds with $\varepsilon_{\max}(n)\to0$. Define $C_{\rm av}(W)$ and $C_{\max}(W)$ as the suprema of the respective achievable-rate sets. Rates use nats per channel use.

For every finite DMC $W$ with no input-cost constraint,
$$C_{\rm av}(W)=C_{\max}(W)=C(W)=\max_{P_X}I(P_X;W),$$
with rates and mutual information measured in nats per channel use.

Let $P_S$ be a probability vector on a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal S$, and define its entropy in nats by

$$H(P_S):=-\sum_{s:P_S(s)>0}P_S(s)\ln P_S(s).$$

For every $R>H(P_S)$, there are deterministic fixed-length codes $f_k:\mathcal S^k\to[M_k]$, $g_k:[M_k]\to\mathcal S^k$ for the IID source $P_S^{\otimes k}$ such that $\Pr[g_k(f_k(S^k))\ne S^k]\to0$ and $\limsup_{k\to\infty}k^{-1}\ln M_k<R$.
For every input probability vector on $\mathcal X^n$ and output $Y^n$ generated by a finite DMC $W^n$, one has $I(X^n;Y^n)\le nC(W)$.

Let $X$ take values in an alphabet $\mathcal X$ of size $m\ge2$, let $Y$ be finite, and let $\widehat X$ be an estimator in the same alphabet generated from $Y$, so the joint pmf factors as $p_{XY\widehat X}=p_{XY}p_{\widehat X|Y}$. Put $P_e=\mathbb P[\widehat X\ne X]$ and define

$$h_2(t):=-t\ln t-(1-t)\ln(1-t),\qquad 0\ln0:=0.$$

Then

$$H(X|Y)\le h_2(P_e)+P_e\ln(m-1)\le \ln2+P_e\ln m.$$

For $m=1$, $X$ is constant and $H(X|Y)=0$.

Let $X,Y,Z$ have a joint pmf on finite alphabets and suppose that, for every $y$ with $p_Y(y)>0$,

$$p_{XZ|y}(x,z)=p_{X|y}(x)p_{Z|y}(z).$$

This is the finite Markov condition $X\to Y\to Z$. Then

$$I(X;Z)\le I(X;Y),$$

with equality if and only if $I(X;Y|Z)=0$, equivalently $X$ and $Y$ are conditionally independent given every positive-mass value of $Z$.

For finite $X,Y,Z$ with a joint pmf,

$$H(X,Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|X,Z),$$

and

$$I(X;Y,Z)=I(X;Z)+I(X;Y|Z).$$

In particular, $I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X|Y)=H(Y)-H(Y|X)$. All terms are finite.

derivations.claim: A zero-entropy finite source is almost surely constant, so constant encoder/decoder maps give a zero-error code even if C(W)=0.
A typical-set source code at rate H+eta has vanishing error and a strict rate margin below rho C.
The maximal-error capacity supremum supplies channel codes at a rate above the source-index rate; restricting to M_k messages preserves correct-decoding events and cannot increase maximal error.
Composition errors are contained in source compression error or channel message error, whose probabilities both vanish; maximal error controls the nonuniform index law.
Data processing, deterministic encoding, the n-letter bound, Fano, and IID entropy give kH <= nC+ln(2)+p_k k ln|S|; divide by k and take limits.
The separate zero-entropy case and strict-rate construction combine with the converse; the positive-entropy equality boundary is left unasserted.

Let $X_0,X_1,\ldots$ be a source over a finite alphabet $\mathcal X$, let $\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be finite, and let $d$ be finite-valued. An $n$-block fixed-length code with $M_n$ messages is a deterministic encoder $f_n:\mathcal X^n\to[M_n]$ and decoder $g_n:[M_n]\to\widehat{\mathcal X}^{\,n}$; its reconstruction is $\widehat X^n=g_n(f_n(X^n))$, its block distortion is [[def-it-single-letter-distortion-and-block-distortion]], and its rate is $n^{-1}\log_2M_n$ bits per source symbol.

Define the expected-distortion operational rate $R_{\mathrm{op}}^{\mathrm{avg}}(D)$ as the infimum of $\limsup_n n^{-1}\log_2M_n$ over code sequences satisfying $\limsup_n\mathbb E d_n(X^n,\widehat X^n)\le D$. Define the positive-slack excess-distortion operational rate $R_{\mathrm{op}}^{\mathrm{slack}}(D)$ by the same rate infimum over code sequences satisfying

$$\text{for every }\varepsilon>0,\qquad \mathbb P\!\left(d_n(X^n,\widehat X^n)>D+\varepsilon\right)\longrightarrow0.$$

The expected and positive-slack excess criteria are separate definitions. An exact-threshold condition $\mathbb P(d_n>D)\to0$ is not part of either definition.

Let $(X_i)_{i\ge0}$ be iid with a pmf on a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal X$, let $\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be finite nonempty, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,d_{\max}]$ be finite nonnegative distortion. For every $D\ge0$, the expected-distortion and positive-slack excess-distortion operational rates of [[def-it-operational-rate-distortion-function]] both equal the finite information rate-distortion function of [[def-it-information-rate-distortion-function]], with value $+\infty$ when $D<D_{\min}$.

A rate $R\ge0$ is **average-error achievable** for $W$ if there are length-$n$ codes for all sufficiently large $n$ with
$$\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{\ln M_n}{n}\ge R,\qquad \varepsilon_{\rm av}(n)\longrightarrow0.$$
It is **maximal-error achievable** if the same condition holds with $\varepsilon_{\max}(n)\to0$. Define $C_{\rm av}(W)$ and $C_{\max}(W)$ as the suprema of the respective achievable-rate sets. Rates use nats per channel use.

For a finite DMC $W$, a **length-$n$ code with $M$ messages** is a pair of maps $e:[M]\to\mathcal X^n$ and $d:\mathcal Y^n\to[M]$, where $n,M\ge1$ and $[M]:=\{1,\ldots,M\}$. A message $m$ is encoded as $e(m)$, passed through the block kernel $W^n$ of [[def-discrete-memoryless-channel]], and decoded as $d(Y^n)$. The encoder and decoder are deterministic; there is no feedback, and no input-cost constraint is imposed.

For a length-$n$ code $(e,d)$, let
$$e_m:=W^n\{y^n:d(y^n)\ne m\mid e(m)\}.$$
Its **average error** is $\varepsilon_{\rm av}:=M^{-1}\sum_{m=1}^M e_m$, corresponding to a uniform message, and its **maximal error** is $\varepsilon_{\max}:=\max_{1\le m\le M}e_m$.

For every finite DMC $W$ with no input-cost constraint,
$$C_{\rm av}(W)=C_{\max}(W)=C(W)=\max_{P_X}I(P_X;W),$$
with rates and mutual information measured in nats per channel use.

Let $S_1,\ldots,S_k$ be IID with law $P_S$ on a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal S$, let $\widehat{\mathcal S}$ be finite nonempty, and let $d:\mathcal S\times\widehat{\mathcal S}\to[0,\infty)$ be finite-valued. For any joint law of $S^k$ and $\widehat S^k$, put $D_k:=\mathbb E d_k(S^k,\widehat S^k)$, using the normalized block distortion of [[def-it-single-letter-distortion-and-block-distortion]]. If $R(D)$ is the finite-alphabet information rate-distortion function in bits from [[def-it-information-rate-distortion-function]], then

$$\ln2\,R(D_k)\le\frac1k I(S^k;\widehat S^k),$$

where mutual information on the right is in nats. The test channel induced by the joint law is feasible at distortion $D_k$, so the rate-distortion minimum is attained there by [[lem-it-finite-rate-distortion-minimum-attained]].

Let the source and reproduction alphabets be finite nonempty sets and let the distortion be finite-valued and nonnegative. The finite-alphabet information rate-distortion function $R(D)$ of [[def-it-information-rate-distortion-function]] is finite and nonincreasing on $[D_{\min},\infty)$, convex there, zero for $D\ge D_{\rm c}:=\min_{\hat x}\mathbb E d(X,\hat x)$, and right-continuous at every feasible distortion, including $D_{\min}$.
For every input probability vector on $\mathcal X^n$ and output $Y^n$ generated by a finite DMC $W^n$, one has $I(X^n;Y^n)\le nC(W)$.

Let $X,Y,Z$ have a joint pmf on finite alphabets and suppose that, for every $y$ with $p_Y(y)>0$,

$$p_{XZ|y}(x,z)=p_{X|y}(x)p_{Z|y}(z).$$

This is the finite Markov condition $X\to Y\to Z$. Then

$$I(X;Z)\le I(X;Y),$$

with equality if and only if $I(X;Y|Z)=0$, equivalently $X$ and $Y$ are conditionally independent given every positive-mass value of $Z$.

Let $p_{XY}$ be a joint probability vector on finite alphabets $\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y$, with marginals $p_X(x):=\sum_y p_{XY}(x,y)$ and $p_Y(y):=\sum_xp_{XY}(x,y)$. The marginals are probability vectors by [[lem-it-finite-marginals-and-conditionals-are-pmfs]]. The joint vector is the outcome-weight function of the canonical finite probability space from [[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]; its coordinate maps are finite random elements in the sense of [[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]. Define mutual information in nats by

$$I(X;Y):=D(p_{XY}\|p_X\otimes p_Y)=\sum_{(x,y):p_{XY}(x,y)>0}p_{XY}(x,y)\ln\frac{p_{XY}(x,y)}{p_X(x)p_Y(y)},$$

where $D$ is the finite KL convention of [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]] and $(p_X\otimes p_Y)(x,y):=p_X(x)p_Y(y)$. Every ratio in the displayed sum is positive and finite: if $p_{XY}(x,y)>0$, then each marginal sum is at least that positive entry. The sum is over finite support, so $I(X;Y)$ is finite. The base-$b$ version replaces $\ln$ by $\log_b$.
For finite probability vectors $p,q$ on the same alphabet, $D(p\|q)\ge0$, and $D(p\|q)=0$ if and only if $p=q$. If $p_i>0=q_i$ for some coordinate, then $D(p\|q)=+\infty$.

For any $b>1$, define each base-$b$ finite information quantity by replacing $\ln$ with $\log_b$ in its defining finite formula. Then

$$H_b(p)=\frac{H(p)}{\ln b},\qquad D_b(p\|q)=\frac{D(p\|q)}{\ln b},$$

For finite $X,Y,Z$ with a joint pmf,

$$H(X,Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|X,Z),$$

and

$$I(X;Y,Z)=I(X;Z)+I(X;Y|Z).$$

In particular, $I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X|Y)=H(Y)-H(Y|X)$. All terms are finite.

derivations.claim: An attained zero-information test channel factors as a product law; some constant reproduction in its finite mixture has distortion at most D, and its IID distortion tail vanishes by the explicit variance bound.
Choose a source-code rate within eta bits of R(D); conversion to nats and n_k/k -> rho place its index rate strictly below Rc.

A maximal-error code exists above Rc by the capacity supremum, and restricting it to M_k messages preserves correct events; its average error remains bounded by maximal error for any nonuniform source index.
On channel success the source reconstruction is unchanged; d_max bounds expected distortion on channel errors, while excess probability is bounded by source excess probability plus channel error.
Single-letter rate-distortion mutual-information bound, Markov data processing, and the n-letter DMC bound yield r(D_k) <= (n_k/k)C(W).
Expected distortion eventually lies below D+epsilon; monotonicity and right-continuity pass the block information bound to r(D) <= rho C.
Bounded distortion and the positive-slack excess criterion imply expected distortion is eventually at most D+epsilon; apply the same monotonicity/continuity argument.
The zero-rate construction, strict-rate achievability, and expected/excess converses prove the claims while leaving positive-rate equality open.

A **finite discrete memoryless channel (DMC)** is the channel sequence [[def-channel-sequence]] with fixed finite nonempty input and output alphabets $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ (with every subset measurable) and one stochastic kernel $W(y\mid x)$ from $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal Y$ ([[def-finite-stochastic-kernel]]). At every blocklength its input and output alphabets are $\mathcal X^n,\mathcal Y^n$, and its block kernel is
$$W^n(y^n\mid x^n):=\prod_{i=1}^n W(y_i\mid x_i).$$
Thus the same single-use transition law is applied independently at each coordinate, conditional on the input word. This page imposes no feedback or input-cost constraint.

For an input probability vector $P_X$ on $\mathcal X$ ([[def-finite-probability-vector]]), let $P_{XY}(x,y):=P_X(x)W(y\mid x)$ and $Q_{P_X}(y):=\sum_xP_X(x)W(y\mid x)$. $$C(W):=\sup_{P_X} I(P_X;W),$$

$$D(p\|q):=\sum_{i:p_i>0}p_i\ln(p_i/q_i),$$
with value $+\infty$ if $p_i>0=q_i$ for some $i$. A matrix $A\in[0,1]^{N\times m}$ is **row-stochastic** when each row sums to one.
